Method of Attack: Steals credentials through fake login prompts overlayed on legitimate website login forms
Takes remote control over mobile device
Uses fake update prompts to install malware
Targets banks with fake login overlays, SMS interception for 2FA codes, keylogging, and cookie stealing
Remote screen streaming and keylogging for social media and messaging apps
UI logging recording clicks, gestures, and all victim actions to bypass Android security flag restrictions
Attack Vector: Malicious dropper apps on Google Play store disguised as legitimate apps
Fake update prompts disguised as Google Play notices or webpages
Dynamic loading of installation logic via additional dex files from command and control servers
AES encryption to obfuscate strings and hide functions from automated scanners
Indicators of Compromise: Dropper apps: 'Codice Fiscale 2022', 'File Manager Small, Lite', 'Recover Audio, Images & Videos', 'Zetter Authentication', 'My Finances Tracker'
Fake update webpages mimicking Google Play
Requests for 'REQUEST_INSTALL_PACKAGES' permission or bypass via browser update prompt
